verdict: Internal integrations work immediately in your own workspace. Public integrations use OAuth, and Notion's docs say the Authorization URL only appears after a public connection is submitted for review. Review timing and criteria are not documented in the page checked.
time: Internal: under 1 hour (estimate). Public: review step exists per the docs; wait not documented.

blockers.text: A public connection must be submitted for review before its Authorization URL is populated.
Users must pick which pages to share at consent, so an empty workspace result is common and not a bug.
Public integrations need company, privacy policy and terms URLs at creation.
Capabilities (read, update, insert) are set on the integration, not per request.

steps: Open my-integrations and create a new integration; set type to Public.
Fill company info, privacy and terms URLs, and add redirect URIs.
Copy the OAuth client ID and secret.
Send users to the authorization URL, then exchange the code at the token endpoint.
Handle the page selection step and test with a workspace you own.
agent: Generate the auth URL and token-exchange code
Run the flow end to end on a test workspace you control
Draft the privacy and terms pages
you: Create the integration under your Notion account
Host the policy pages on your domain
uncertain: Review criteria and duration for public connections were not found.
Whether company, privacy policy and terms URLs are required at creation was not confirmed.
Marketplace or gallery listing is a separate process and was not checked.
